sources.entry: ClearanceKit - File-access control for macOS that protects sensitive user data from supply-chain attacks using Endpoint Security.

summary.one_liner: ClearanceKit is a macOS file-access control app that uses Endpoint Security to block unapproved processes from reading or changing protected paths, with policies keyed to code signing identity.
summary.what_it_does: It intercepts file-system events on macOS (opens, renames, deletes, hard links, creates, truncations, copies, directory reads, data exchanges, clones) and enforces per-process policies on paths the user marks as protected. A process without an explicit allow rule is denied access to a protected path. Jail rules confine a named process to a set of path prefixes and deny everything outside them. Denied events appear in a SwiftUI interface where the user can review them and build policy. Policies reference a Team ID and Signing ID rather than file paths or hashes, so they persist across software updates. Policies can also be delivered by MDM through managed preferences, and ancestor-based allowlists let rules trust a process based on its parent chain.
use_cases: protect SSH keys and cloud credentials from package install scripts
block unknown processes from reading browser cookies or messages
confine a tool to a fixed set of directories with a jail rule
review denied file access events and build policy from them
deploy file-access policies to managed Macs via MDM
lock down config files so only specific signed binaries can modify them
how_to_run: Download the latest DMG from the Releases page
Open the DMG and drag clearancekit to Applications
Launch the app and open the Setup tab
Click Activate Extension and approve it in System Settings
Grant Full Disk Access to the system extension when prompted
notable: Policies bind to Team ID and Signing ID rather than file hashes, so they survive updates
Jail rules confine a process to specific path prefixes regardless of other rules
Ancestor allowlists trust a process based on its parent chain
MDM support via managed preference profiles with a reference .mobileconfig
Zero third-party dependencies, using only Apple frameworks
caveats: Requires an Apple Developer account with the Endpoint Security entitlement, plus Developer ID provisioning profiles, to build from source
Needs system extension approval and Full Disk Access on first launch
Does not restrict execution events; it only governs file access (no lockdown mode like Santa)
No auto-update; updates must be checked manually on the Releases page
